task.title: Enter a date, even one you are not sure of
task.shortdesc: Enter an exact date, a part of a date, or a date you can only guess, and read how the app has understood it.

context.p: Every box that asks for a date works the same way. A good researcher enters what the record says. A date you are not sure of is entered as not sure, never as a guess.

step.cmd: In a date, type the day and the year, and choose the month from the list.

info.p: You can leave out the day, or the day and the month.

stepresult.p: A line under the date says how the app reads it, such as Reads as 21 April 1816.

step.cmd: To say how sure you are, turn on .

stepresult.p: Two lists show. offers , , , , , and . offers , and .

step.cmd: Choose the kind of date, and how much you know.

info.p: For with , the form shows two year boxes with the word and between them. Type both years.

stepresult.p: The line under the boxes follows what you type, such as Reads as between 1813 and 1814.

step.cmd: To type the whole date in one box, turn on .

info.p: The line under the box shows how the app reads what you typed. Words such as about, before and between work. lists them.

result.p: A calendar other than the Gregorian one is behind the button . It has the Julian, Hebrew and French Republican calendars. explains when to use them.
The app does not check that a day exists. A date such as 31 February 1900 is kept as you typed it. Each date box also has a small help button of its own.
